label: Original/delimiter steps after l/q/w/d have appeared, plus input j
explanation: Mostly fires during the original phase and at <DEL> (32% of <DEL> steps, 22% of activation mass), once one of the tokens l, q, w or d has been input. Strongest right after l, about 0.45 rate when prev_tok = l, then q and w; it decays over the next couple of steps and builds up through the sequence. Input j also triggers it (52% rate), in any phase, and j makes up much of the top quartile. The top activations are at <DEL> in sequences that start with j and contain l/q, followed by the j echoed back at the first copy step. It never fires at t=0 and is weak in the copy phase apart from j inputs. Precision is low (about 0.37): many steps after l/q/w/d stay silent, so the feature looks like a graded sum of evidence from recent tokens rather than a clean boolean.
